---
title: "First Look at a Raster File: Dimensions, Bands, and NoData"
date: 2026-09-06
categories: [tool, raster, bilingual]
description: "Upload a GeoTIFF and get an instant summary — dimensions, resolution, band count, CRS, NoData, and per-band min/max/mean — in Python and R on the same map."
---

A vector file's first look answers "how many features, what shape, what
CRS." A raster's is a different set of numbers entirely: how big is the
grid, how many bands does each pixel carry, what does one pixel cover
on the ground, and which value means "no data here" rather than a real
measurement.

Get those wrong and everything downstream is wrong too — a slope
calculation that treats -9999 as a very steep cliff, a mean elevation
dragged down by a border of NoData pixels, a band mistaken for degrees
Celsius when it's really reflectance times 10,000.

Just want the summary, without the rest of the reading? Use the
[standalone tool](/tools/raster-inspector.html) — same engine, less
prose.

## 1. Upload your file

A single `.tif` or `.tiff` — no sidecars, unlike a shapefile.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable uploadedFiles = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
uploadControl = WebGeoDS.Upload.createControl({
  label: "Upload",
  onChange: (files) => { mutable uploadedFiles = files; }
```


## 2. Why start with a summary?

Eight numbers, each answering a question that's otherwise easy to get
wrong by assumption:

- **Dimensions** — width × height in pixels. Determines how much work
  any pixel-by-pixel operation actually is, and whether a "small" file
  is small in bytes but enormous in pixel count (or the reverse).
- **Bands** — one grid of numbers, or several stacked together (RGB,
  a multispectral stack, a time series). Some checks and most
  visualizations only make sense once you know how many there are.
- **CRS** — same coordinate reference system concept as a vector file.
  A missing CRS is reported as genuinely unknown, not silently
  relabeled as WGS84 — the map still needs *some* projection to place
  the footprint, so that assumption is shown separately, labeled as a
  display choice rather than folded into the CRS field itself.
- **Resolution** — the ground distance one pixel actually covers, in
  the file's own CRS units. A 30 (Landsat-scale) versus a 0.001
  (sub-meter) changes what questions the data can even answer.
- **Data type** — `uint8`, `int16`, `float32`, ... . The single most
  common source of a "why are all my values 0 or wildly wrong"
  surprise: an integer type storing values that were meant to be
  divided by a scale factor, or a float column silently truncated by
  being written back as an integer type.
- **NoData** — the sentinel value marking "no measurement here" (often
  `-9999`, `0`, or a type's max value) — as fundamental to a raster as
  a null is to a table column, and just as easy to accidentally treat
  as a real number if it isn't checked first.
- **Bounds** — the same bounding-box sanity check as a vector file:
  numbers wildly outside -180..180 / -90..90 are the CRS-mismatch tell,
  here too.
- **Value range** — the per-band min/max/mean, with NoData pixels
  correctly excluded. The fastest way to catch a unit mistake (a
  "temperature in Celsius" band whose values run from 200 to 320 is
  actually Kelvin) before it reaches an analysis.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two cards side by side, same reasoning as the vector article: a
// combined "total pixel count" wouldn't mean anything, but seeing the
// two engines' numbers agree (or noticing where the CRS string or
// data type label doesn't) is itself the point — see section 5.
statCard = (label, s) => {
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.style.flex = "1";
  wrap.style.minWidth = "260px";

  const heading = document.createElement("div");
  heading.className = "webgeods-label";
  heading.textContent = label;
  wrap.appendChild(heading);

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";
  wrap.appendChild(box);

  const row = (rowLabel, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = rowLabel;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s) {
    row("Dimensions", "—");
    return wrap;
  }

  const MAX_BANDS_SHOWN = 6;
  const bandLines = s.bandStats.slice(0, MAX_BANDS_SHOWN).map((b) =>
    b.min === null
      ? `Band ${b.band}: all NoData`
      : `Band ${b.band}: ${b.min} to ${b.max} (mean ${b.mean})`
  );
  if (s.bandStats.length > MAX_BANDS_SHOWN) {
    bandLines.push(`… and ${s.bandStats.length - MAX_BANDS_SHOWN} more band(s)`);
  }

  row("Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`);
  row("Bands", String(s.bandCount));
  row("CRS", s.crs === null || s.crs === undefined ? `Unknown ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : s.crs);
  if (s.displayCrsAssumption) {
    row("Display assumption", `${s.displayCrsAssumption} — map only, not a fact about the file`);
  }
  row("Resolution", s.resolution.join(" × "));
  // terra's datatype() returns "" for a raster built directly from a
  // matrix (the fallback example, no GDAL file behind it — nothing to
  // report a storage type FROM) rather than a placeholder string —
  // shown as "—" here for the same reason every other "nothing to
  // show" value on this page is, not blank space that reads as a
  // rendering bug.
  row("Data type", s.dtype || "—");
  row("NoData", s.nodata === null || s.nodata === undefined ? "None declared" : String(s.nodata));
  row("Bounds", s.bounds.join(", "));
  row("Value range", bandLines.join(" · "));

  return wrap;
}
```

## 4. Inspect: summarize your file

Run the same summary in Python or R on the current data (your file
uploaded above, or the built-in example below).

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Python

```{.webgeods-python #raster-inspect-py}
#| package: rasterio, numpy
import rasterio
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.io import MemoryFile
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds
import numpy as np

path = None
for candidate in ["/uploaded.tif"]:
    try:
        with rasterio.open(candidate):
            path = candidate
            break
    except Exception:
        pass

# No file uploaded yet: a small synthetic hill built directly in
# memory (rasterio.io.MemoryFile — no virtual-filesystem path needed
# for a fallback), with one deliberately-NoData corner pixel so the
# NoData row below has something real to show.
memfile = None
if path is None:
    n = 20
    xs = np.arange(n)
    ys = np.arange(n)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    elevation = (100 + 40 * np.exp(-((X - 10) ** 2 + (Y - 10) ** 2) / 30)).astype("float32")
    elevation[0, 0] = -9999
    transform = from_origin(12.40, 41.95, 0.005, 0.005)
    memfile = MemoryFile()
    with memfile.open(
        driver="GTiff", height=n, width=n, count=1,
        dtype="float32", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=transform, nodata=-9999
    ) as dst:
        dst.write(elevation, 1)
    path = memfile.name

with rasterio.open(path) as src:
    # A missing CRS is reported as genuinely unknown, not silently
    # relabeled as WGS84 — "no CRS" and "WGS84" are different facts,
    # and blurring them defeats the point of a tool whose whole job is
    # telling you what's actually true about the file. EPSG:4326 is
    # still used internally (crs_for_transform) to place the footprint
    # on the map — that's a display convenience, reported separately
    # below as display_crs_assumption, never folded into the "crs"
    # field itself.
    crs_warning = None
    display_crs_assumption = None
    if src.crs is not None:
        crs_for_transform = src.crs
        crs_label = str(src.crs)
    else:
        crs_for_transform = "EPSG:4326"
        crs_label = None
        crs_warning = "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
        display_crs_assumption = "EPSG:4326"

    # Per-band min/max/mean, NoData pixels excluded via masked=True —
    # a band that's entirely NoData reports nulls instead of a bogus
    # min/max computed from an empty array.
    band_stats = []
    for i in range(1, src.count + 1):
        band = src.read(i, masked=True)
        has_valid = band.count() > 0
        band_stats.append({
            "band": i,
            "min": round(float(band.min()), 4) if has_valid else None,
            "max": round(float(band.max()), 4) if has_valid else None,
            "mean": round(float(band.mean()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        })

    bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in src.bounds]
    try:
        wgs84_bounds = transform_bounds(crs_for_transform, "EPSG:4326", *src.bounds)
    except Exception:
        wgs84_bounds = src.bounds

    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = wgs84_bounds
    footprint = {
        "type": "FeatureCollection",
        "features": [{
            "type": "Feature",
            "properties": {"name": "raster footprint"},
            "geometry": {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "coordinates": [[[minx, miny], [maxx, miny], [maxx, maxy], [minx, maxy], [minx, miny]]]
            }
        }]
    }

    summary = {
        "width": src.width,
        "height": src.height,
        "bandCount": src.count,
        "crs": crs_label,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "displayCrsAssumption": display_crs_assumption,
        "nodata": src.nodata,
        "resolution": [round(float(r), 6) for r in src.res],
        "dtype": src.dtypes[0],
        "bounds": bounds,
        "bandStats": band_stats,
    }

if memfile is not None:
    memfile.close()

{
    "summary": summary,
    "footprint": footprint
}
```

## R

```{.webgeods-r #raster-inspect-r}
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

if (is.null(path)) {
  # Same synthetic hill as the Python fallback — built directly as a
  # SpatRaster from a plain matrix via rast(), with the extent set
  # explicitly afterward, rather than through a file: no virtual
  # filesystem needed for this side either.
  n <- 20
  xs <- 0:(n - 1)
  ys <- 0:(n - 1)
  elevation <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
  elevation[1, 1] <- NA
  r <- rast(elevation, crs = "EPSG:4326")
  ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)
} else {
  r <- rast(path)
}

# A missing CRS is reported as genuinely unknown, not silently
# relabeled as WGS84 (same reasoning as the Python cell above). terra
# reports a missing CRS as an empty string, not NA — checked directly
# rather than through an sf-style is.na() test (this cell no longer
# depends on sf at all, see the footprint construction below).
# was_missing_crs is captured BEFORE crs(r) is mutated below, since
# that mutation is only there to give the footprint reprojection
# something to work with — the label itself must stay NULL regardless
# of what crs(r) reports afterward.
was_missing_crs <- crs(r) == ""
crs_warning <- NULL
display_crs_assumption <- NULL
if (was_missing_crs) {
  crs_warning <- "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
  display_crs_assumption <- "EPSG:4326"
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
}

# crs(r, describe = TRUE) resolves to an EPSG code when the CRS is one
# GDAL recognizes (the common case); crs(r, proj = TRUE) is the
# fallback for anything else. See section 5 — this is one of the
# genuine format divergences from Python's str(src.crs). Skipped
# entirely when the CRS was missing — describing the EPSG:4326 just
# assigned above would misreport it as the file's own CRS.
crs_label <- if (was_missing_crs) {
  NULL
} else {
  crs_desc <- crs(r, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(r, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

band_count <- nlyr(r)
res_xy <- res(r)
e <- ext(r)
bounds <- c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax)

# jsonlite::toJSON() treats every length-1 vector as a single-element
# array by default — a genuine scalar (a width, a CRS string) needs an
# explicit jsonlite::unbox() to serialize as one. ub()/ub_if() below
# are just that, plus a NULL passthrough for optional fields (see
# geospatial-file-inspection.qmd for the full reasoning on why this,
# not toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE), is the safer default).
ub <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(x)
ub_if <- function(cond, x) if (cond) jsonlite::unbox(x) else NULL

# global(..., na.rm = TRUE) computes per-band stats directly — terra
# reads the file's declared NoData value and excludes those pixels
# automatically (confirmed: a -9999 sentinel pixel never pollutes the
# min below), the same way rasterio's masked=True does. Unlike
# rasterio, though, the sentinel value itself isn't exposed anywhere
# afterward either — see section 5.
stats <- global(r, c("min", "max", "mean"), na.rm = TRUE)
band_stats <- lapply(seq_len(band_count), function(i) {
  has_valid <- is.finite(stats$min[i])
  list(
    band = jsonlite::unbox(i),
    min = ub_if(has_valid, round(stats$min[i], 4)),
    max = ub_if(has_valid, round(stats$max[i], 4)),
    mean = ub_if(has_valid, round(stats$mean[i], 4))
  )
})

# MapLibre/GeoJSON require WGS84 — the bounding box is reprojected via
# terra's own vect()/project() (no sf needed) the same way the
# summary's own "bounds" field stays in the file's native CRS (same
# reasoning as the vector article). geom() reads the reprojected
# polygon's coordinates back out as a plain matrix.
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("raster footprint")),
    geometry = list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
      coordinates = list(footprint_coords)
    )
  ))
)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
  height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
  bandCount = jsonlite::unbox(band_count),
  crs = ub(crs_label),
  crsWarning = ub(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = ub(display_crs_assumption),
  nodata = NULL,
  resolution = c(round(res_xy[1], 6), round(res_xy[2], 6)),
  # datatype(r) returns one type PER BAND (terra allows different bands
  # to carry different types, even if real files rarely do) -- a plain
  # unbox() on a multi-band raster throws "Tried to unbox a vector of
  # length N". [1] takes the first band's type, same convention as
  # rasterio's own src.dtypes[0] on the Python side.
  dtype = jsonlite::unbox(datatype(r)[1]),
  bounds = unname(round(bounds, 6)),
  bandStats = band_stats
)

# Round-tripped through JSON once more, whole-object — same reasoning
# as the vector article: R's atomic vectors don't cross the webR->JS
# bridge as plain JS arrays on their own the way a jsonlite-parsed
# list does.
result <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

:::

## 5. Same spatial question, two languages

Python and R read the same file through the same underlying GDAL, but
the two engines disagree in ways a vector file's `sf`/GeoPandas split
never surfaces:

**Python** (rasterio)

```python
src.width, src.height     # dimensions
src.count                 # band count
src.crs                   # CRS
src.res                   # pixel resolution
src.dtypes[0]              # data type, as declared in the file
src.nodata                 # the NoData sentinel value itself
src.read(i, masked=True)  # one band, NoData pixels masked out
```

**R** (terra)

```r
ncol(r), nrow(r), nlyr(r)   # dimensions + band count
crs(r, describe = TRUE)     # CRS, resolved to an EPSG code when GDAL recognizes one
res(r)                      # pixel resolution
datatype(r)[1]               # terra's own type code, one per band -- [1] mirrors dtypes[0]
# no direct equivalent — see below
global(r, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)  # NoData pixels already excluded
```

Three genuine divergences, not just naming differences:

- **CRS formatting** — same issue as the vector article's `st_crs()`
  vs GeoPandas footnote: when GDAL can resolve the file's CRS to a
  known EPSG code, `crs(r, describe = TRUE)` gives exactly that
  (`"EPSG:4326"`, matching Python here) — but for anything it can't
  match to a registry entry, the fallback is a `+proj=...` string,
  a different format entirely from `str(src.crs)`.[^raster-crs-format]
- **Data type** — closer to Python than `stars` was: `datatype(r)`
  does reflect the file's actual storage type, just under terra's own
  naming convention (`"FLT4S"` for a 4-byte signed float, `"INT2U"`
  for an unsigned 16-bit integer, ...) rather than GDAL's own
  descriptive names (`"float32"`, `"uint16"`) the way rasterio's
  `dtypes[0]` reports them. A real format difference, not a loss of
  information the way it was with `stars` — though `datatype(r)`
  itself returns one type *per band* (terra allows different bands to
  carry different types), so both sides here report only the first
  band's type, `dtypes[0]` and `datatype(r)[1]` respectively.
- **NoData retention** — `rast()` reads the file's declared NoData
  value and excludes those pixels automatically wherever a reduction
  is computed (confirmed: a `-9999` sentinel pixel never pollutes
  `global(..., "min")` above), the same way rasterio's `masked=True`
  does — but the sentinel value itself isn't exposed anywhere
  afterward. rasterio keeps it directly on `src.nodata`; terra
  doesn't have an equally direct equivalent for a file already open.
  That's why the R card's "NoData" row never shows anything but "None
  declared," even on a file that clearly has one — it isn't wrong,
  the exclusion already happened, there's just no simple accessor left
  to report the raw number by.

[^raster-crs-format]: A GeoTIFF's own embedded CRS often resolves to a
human-readable name in GDAL's metadata (e.g. `"WGS 84"`), which
`crs(r, describe = TRUE)` still maps back to its EPSG code when one
exists — while an unusual or locally-defined CRS with no registry
match falls back to a PROJ string on the R side, with no equivalent
fallback needed on Python's, since `str(src.crs)` already prints
whatever GDAL gave it either way. Worth checking which form you're
looking at before assuming a mismatch means an actual problem.

## 6. A raster with no declared CRS

The reusable cell pair above already builds a small synthetic hill
with one NoData pixel whenever nothing has been uploaded — click
**▶ Run** on both languages in section 4 to see it. This button swaps
in the same raster, minus the CRS, to see the CRS row switch to
"Unknown" and a separate "Display assumption" row appear below
it.[^raster-crs-missing]

[^raster-crs-missing]: An unreferenced raster isn't rare in practice —
a sensor's raw output, or a file exported by a tool that never wrote a
CRS tag at all. Nothing about the pixel *values* is wrong in that
case; only where they sit on the earth is unknown until someone
supplies it, which is exactly the situation the warning exists to
flag before a map silently plots it in the wrong place (or, for
`sf`/GeoPandas, refuses to reproject it at all).


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pyNoCrsExampleCode = `import rasterio
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.io import MemoryFile
import numpy as np

n = 20
xs = np.arange(n)
ys = np.arange(n)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
elevation = (100 + 40 * np.exp(-((X - 10) ** 2 + (Y - 10) ** 2) / 30)).astype("float32")
elevation[0, 0] = -9999
transform = from_origin(12.40, 41.95, 0.005, 0.005)

# crs deliberately omitted — the whole point of this example.
memfile = MemoryFile()
with memfile.open(
    driver="GTiff", height=n, width=n, count=1,
    dtype="float32", transform=transform, nodata=-9999
) as dst:
    dst.write(elevation, 1)

with rasterio.open(memfile.name) as src:
    crs_warning = None
    display_crs_assumption = None
    if src.crs is not None:
        crs_label = str(src.crs)
    else:
        crs_label = None
        crs_warning = "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
        display_crs_assumption = "EPSG:4326"

    band_stats = []
    for i in range(1, src.count + 1):
        band = src.read(i, masked=True)
        has_valid = band.count() > 0
        band_stats.append({
            "band": i,
            "min": round(float(band.min()), 4) if has_valid else None,
            "max": round(float(band.max()), 4) if has_valid else None,
            "mean": round(float(band.mean()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        })

    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = src.bounds
    footprint = {
        "type": "FeatureCollection",
        "features": [{
            "type": "Feature",
            "properties": {"name": "raster footprint"},
            "geometry": {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "coordinates": [[[minx, miny], [maxx, miny], [maxx, maxy], [minx, maxy], [minx, miny]]]
            }
        }]
    }

    summary = {
        "width": src.width, "height": src.height, "bandCount": src.count,
        "crs": crs_label, "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "displayCrsAssumption": display_crs_assumption, "nodata": src.nodata,
        "resolution": [round(float(r), 6) for r in src.res], "dtype": src.dtypes[0],
        "bounds": [round(float(b), 6) for b in src.bounds], "bandStats": band_stats,
    }

memfile.close()

{"summary": summary, "footprint": footprint}`
rNoCrsExampleCode = `library(terra)

n <- 20
xs <- 0:(n - 1)
ys <- 0:(n - 1)
elevation <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
elevation[1, 1] <- NA
# crs deliberately omitted from rast() -- the whole point of this example.
r <- rast(elevation)
ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)

was_missing_crs <- crs(r) == ""
crs_warning <- NULL
display_crs_assumption <- NULL
if (was_missing_crs) {
  crs_warning <- "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
  display_crs_assumption <- "EPSG:4326"
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
}
crs_label <- if (was_missing_crs) {
  NULL
} else {
  crs_desc <- crs(r, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(r, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

res_xy <- res(r)
e <- ext(r)
bounds <- c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax)

stats <- global(r, c("min", "max", "mean"), na.rm = TRUE)
band_stats <- list(list(
  band = jsonlite::unbox(1),
  min = jsonlite::unbox(round(stats$min[1], 4)),
  max = jsonlite::unbox(round(stats$max[1], 4)),
  mean = jsonlite::unbox(round(stats$mean[1], 4))
))

bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("raster footprint")),
    geometry = list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
      coordinates = list(footprint_coords)
    )
  ))
)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)), height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)), bandCount = jsonlite::unbox(1),
  crs = NULL, crsWarning = jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = jsonlite::unbox(display_crs_assumption), nodata = NULL,
  resolution = c(round(res_xy[1], 6), round(res_xy[2], 6)), dtype = jsonlite::unbox(datatype(r)[1]),
  bounds = unname(round(bounds, 6)), bandStats = band_stats
)

result <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)`
```

## 7. Where to next

A summary is a starting point:

- **Just needed the numbers?** The
  [standalone Raster Inspector](/tools/raster-inspector.html) has the
  same summary, no reading required.
- **Working with vector data instead?** Start with
  [First Look at a Geospatial File](geospatial-file-inspection.qmd) —
  the same idea, for GeoJSON and Shapefile.
- **Need to combine two bands into a result** (a difference map, a
  Normalized Difference like NDVI)? See
  [Raster Band Math](raster-band-math.qmd), or the standalone
  [Raster Calculator](/tools/raster-calculator.html).
